messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Compulsory and pre-school education and Children in Hesse during the 1960s, matching this research need: survey data on political socialization in preschool children and parents, focusing on family authority, attitudes to authority and punishment, child-rearing practices, role models like police, and demographic background
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: dataset political socialization preschool children parents Hesse 1960s authority punishment police survey
GESIS politische Sozialisation Vorschulkinder Eltern Hessen 1960er Polizei Strafe Erziehung Datensatz
Compulsory and pre-school education and Children in Hesse 1960s dataset
action.query: dataset political socialization preschool children parents Hesse 1960s authority punishment police survey

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Patterns of Child Rearing, 1951–1958","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/CTETA1","justification":"Highly relevant historical survey dataset examining parental child-rearing practices, family authority, discipline, punishment, and demographic characteristics. Interviews cover parental decisions about child training, rewards and punishments, children's aggression, parental reactions, and family responsibilities. Although collected in the United States during the 1950s rather than Hesse in the 1960s, it provides valuable comparative evidence on family authority and early childhood political socialization."},{"title":"Three-Wave Political Socialization Panel Survey of Children in the San Francisco East Bay Area, 1968–1969 (ICPSR 2341)","url_or_doi":"https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/ICPSR/studies/2341","justification":"Historical survey dataset directly investigating children's political socialization during the late 1960s. Measures political opinions and their development over time, alongside demographic variables including age, sex, religion, parental occupation, education, and socioeconomic background. Particularly useful for investigating how children acquire political attitudes and orientations toward authority. The geographical coverage is California rather than Hesse, and the study is not specifically restricted to preschool children."},{"title":"Politics and the English Child, 1969","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5255/UKDA-SN-55-1","justification":"Highly relevant 1969 survey dataset exploring children's political attitudes, perceptions of authority, and family influences on political socialization. Includes children's attitudes toward police, political leaders, schools, and other institutions, as well as political discussions within families, parental political affiliations, religion, parental occupations, education, age, sex, and social class. Particularly valuable for studying police as authority figures and the relationship between family background and political attitudes. Covers English schoolchildren rather than preschool children in Hesse."}]}
